diagrams.title: From Remittance Exception to Earned Contingency
diagrams.subtitle: Five operating steps; provider recoveries never become operator revenue.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Operate under provider authorization and HIPAA Business Associate Agreements where required by 45 CFR § 164.504(e). The initial payment is an actual remittance; QPA is a separate statutory benchmark and must not be substituted for the cash baseline. Apply current CMS instructions and controlling rules to each filing rather than hardcoding fee schedules or batching criteria.
diagrams.caption: Separate eligibility, deadline preservation, evidence, collection, and revenue recognition. No award amount enters the earned-fee ledger before the relevant incremental cash is collected.

stages.label: Reconcile the baseline
stages.detail: Ingest authorized 835 ERA records, CARC/RARC codes, claim identifiers, initial allowed amounts, and payment dates. Match payer cash to the claim and preserve the reported QPA separately; denial codes alone do not establish an underpayment or federal eligibility.

stages.label: Select the payment rail
stages.detail: Verify service setting, network status, coverage, plan funding, applicable state law, and any All-Payer Model Agreement. Route eligible federal disputes under 42 U.S.C. § 300gg-111 and 45 CFR § 149.510; segregate state-process cases before incurring federal filing costs.

stages.label: Preserve the deadlines
stages.detail: Track receipt of initial payment or denial, the separate 30-business-day period to start open negotiation, and the 30-business-day negotiation period. If unresolved, track the four-business-day IDR initiation window after negotiation ends; initiation is distinct from entity selection and later offer submission.

stages.label: Build the offer packet
stages.detail: Use QPA, relevant clinical acuity, case complexity, and permitted contracting evidence. Licensed FAIR Health material requires field-level screening; do not submit usual-and-customary charges, billed charges, or public payer rates as prohibited benchmarks under 42 U.S.C. § 300gg-111(c)(5)(D).

stages.label: Collect and allocate
stages.detail: Reconcile additional payer receipts and confirmed entity fee refunds. Fee base equals incremental cash above the initial payer payment, less unrecovered CMS administrative fees, entity fees, and agreed casework costs, floored at zero. Multiply that base by the contracted share; keep provider-owned cash out of operator revenue.

diagrams.title: A Favorable Determination Is Not Collected Cash
diagrams.subtitle: One fixed referral cohort, five nested counts, one observation date.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Illustrative cohort counts, not observed performance or the canonical annual revenue model. Every stage is a subset of the preceding stage. Negotiated settlements leave this arbitration funnel and enter a separate collection ledger. Unpaid awards remain receivables or disputed items, not earned contingency revenue under this cash-conditioned model.
diagrams.caption: The example has 420 favorable determinations but only 280 cases with incremental cash received: a 66.7% paid share of favorable cases and a 28.0% referral-to-cash conversion.

stages.label: Referred claims
stages.detail: Freeze a dated intake cohort with unique claim identifiers, provider authority, payer remittance records, and bank reconciliation links; count each dispute unit once.

stages.label: Federal-eligible claims
stages.detail: Document federal eligibility and usable records for 700 claims. Exclude the other 300 from this cohort's federal filing path because routing or documentation requirements were not satisfied.

stages.label: Timely initiated disputes
stages.detail: Carry 560 unresolved, timely initiated disputes forward after open negotiation. The remaining 140 include settlements and operational exits; track their outcomes separately rather than labeling them arbitration losses.

stages.label: Favorable determinations
stages.detail: Record 420 favorable determinations by the observation date. Split the other 140 among pending, adverse, and dismissed cases in the case ledger; do not treat every non-favorable observation as a final merits loss.

stages.label: Incremental cash received
stages.detail: Match incremental receipts for 280 favorable cases to bank activity. The other 140 favorable cases have no matched incremental cash at this cutoff. Partial receipts support fees only on their actual net collected amount.

diagrams.title: $505,000 Earned Fees to $217,150 Owner Profit
diagrams.subtitle: Six bars reconcile the canonical Base-Case 43.0% net margin.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Canonical endpoints are $505,000 annual operator revenue and $217,150 owner profit. Cost splits and the supporting recovery pool are illustrative engineering assumptions. Example fee base: $2,200,000 incremental provider cash collected minus $80,000 unrecovered administrative/entity fees minus $100,000 provider-borne casework costs equals $2,020,000; a 25% retained share produces $505,000 earned operator revenue. Those two provider-borne deductions are outside the operator expense bars and must not be deducted twice. No baseline provider collections are included.
diagrams.caption: $505,000 − $156,000 − $30,000 − $36,000 − $65,850 = $217,150. Owner profit divided by earned operator revenue equals 43.0%. The first and last bars are totals; the four middle bars are negative changes, not additional revenue.

stages.label: Earned operator revenue
stages.detail: Recognize the operator's earned 25% share of the $2,020,000 net incremental collection pool. Where the operator is an agent under ASC 606, exclude provider proceeds and pass-through recoveries from recognized revenue; document the principal-versus-agent assessment.

stages.label: Variable delivery labor
stages.detail: Illustrative operator-funded contractor delivery labor and specialist support, separate from provider-borne casework already deducted in the fee-base calculation. Owner distributions are not a second labor deduction.

stages.label: Systems and protected storage
stages.detail: Budget $2,500 monthly for contracted secure infrastructure, 835 ingestion, access logging, deadline automation, and licensed evidence tools. Verify business-associate terms before any service receives protected health information.

stages.label: Core operating overhead
stages.detail: Budget $3,000 monthly for insurance, accounting, workspace, and routine administration. Combined with systems, $5,500 monthly fixed overhead sits within the supplied $1,800–$10,500 core operating budget range.

stages.label: Acquisition and variable support
stages.detail: Allocate illustrative non-fixed acquisition, provider onboarding, and transaction support costs. Total operator expenses are $287,850 annually; the monthly core budget range does not represent all-in expenses including variable delivery and acquisition.

stages.label: Owner net profit
stages.detail: Canonical Base-Case annual residual for the 1 FT + 2 C pod. Preserve the scorecard's owner-profit definition; do not silently recast this figure as a provider recovery amount, salary figure, or award-value margin.

diagrams.title: Compare Cash Yield, Not Headline Awards
diagrams.subtitle: Illustrative earned fees per referred claim on eligible federal rails.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Each bar uses an independent ten-referral cohort, including referrals producing zero cash, and a hypothetical 25% retained share. Net recovery pools already exclude initial payer collections, unrecovered administrative/entity fees, and agreed casework costs. These are comparison assumptions, not specialty benchmarks, expected returns, or a weighted bridge to annual scorecard revenue. Operator overhead remains to be deducted.
diagrams.caption: Normalize collections to all referred claims so rejected claims, losses, and unpaid awards reduce yield. Specialty labels do not establish jurisdiction or eligibility.

stages.label: Emergency physician
stages.detail: A $6,000 net incremental cash pool across ten referrals produces $1,500 operator fees at 25%. Screen emergency service circumstances, payer coverage, and the applicable state or federal payment route before filing.

stages.label: Facility anesthesia
stages.detail: An $8,000 net incremental cash pool across ten referrals produces $2,000 operator fees at 25%. Verify the participating-facility context and applicable ancillary service protections rather than relying on the specialty code alone.

stages.label: Facility radiology
stages.detail: A $4,000 net incremental cash pool across ten referrals produces $1,000 operator fees at 25%. Separate professional and technical components, validate service identifiers, and prevent duplicate recovery across component claims.

stages.label: Facility pathology
stages.detail: A $3,200 net incremental cash pool across ten referrals produces $800 operator fees at 25%. Validate covered facility-linked services and permitted batching criteria; similar specialty labels do not make every claim batchable.

stages.label: Covered air ambulance
stages.detail: A $24,000 net incremental cash pool across ten referrals produces $6,000 operator fees at 25%. Apply the distinct air-ambulance requirements in 45 CFR § 149.520 and 42 U.S.C. § 300gg-112; exclude ground ambulance claims from this federal comparison.

diagrams.title: Four Checks Before Federal Filing
diagrams.subtitle: Explicit stop, reroute, and proceed outcomes preserve fees and deadlines.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Evaluate the checks in sequence for each proposed dispute or batch. Statutory anchors include 42 U.S.C. § 300gg-111, 45 CFR §§ 149.30 and 149.510, and HIPAA business-associate requirements in 45 CFR § 164.504(e). Verify current CMS operational guidance and applicable court orders when configuring deadline, fee, and batching rules.
diagrams.caption: A missing fact is a work item, not permission to file. Every negative branch must identify the responsible person, next action, and remaining deadline.

stages.label: Authority and protected records
stages.detail: Yes: retain provider representation authority, required BAA terms, access controls, and relevant records. No: stop protected-data ingestion and filing until authority and handling arrangements are established; use de-identified samples for system testing.

stages.label: Federal payment jurisdiction
stages.detail: Yes: document covered service circumstances and why federal IDR applies. No: route to the applicable state process, contractual appeal, or other supported channel. Do not equate self-funded ERISA status with automatic eligibility or fully insured status with automatic exclusion.

stages.label: Timing and batch validity
stages.detail: Yes: retain negotiation notices, business-day calculations, timely initiation evidence, and current batch criteria. No: remove incompatible claims or stop the filing. Apply the 90-calendar-day same-party, same-or-similar-item cooling-off restriction and its applicable post-period initiation window; never reset clocks through relabeling.

stages.label: Evidence and collection economics
stages.detail: Proceed only with a supportable offer and a positive risk-adjusted net collection estimate. Budget CMS administrative fees as non-refundable and losing or ineligible cases as unrecovered entity-fee exposure. Credit prevailing-party entity refunds only when confirmed; apply dismissal-specific rules rather than presuming a refund. Otherwise renegotiate, correct, or decline.

diagrams.title: Three People Launch; Five People Scale
diagrams.subtitle: Clear ownership separates filing execution from cash reconciliation.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Canonical Conservative: $110,000 revenue × 30% = $33,000 owner profit with 1 FT + 2 C. Canonical Base-Case: $505,000 × 43.0% = $217,150 with the same three-person structure. Canonical Scaled: $900,000 × 56% = $504,000 with 2 FT + 3 C. Revenue means earned operator contingency, not provider collections. Seats four and five are additions only in the Scaled configuration.
diagrams.caption: FT means full-time seat; C means contractor seat, not assumed full-time capacity. Assign a named backup for every deadline and keep evidence decisions separate from receipt confirmation.

stages.label: Owner and recovery lead
stages.detail: Own provider contracts, jurisdiction exceptions, offer authority, fee-base definitions, and operating economics. Maintain the exception queue and engage appropriately qualified specialists when a matter exceeds the team's authorized scope.

stages.label: Claims and deadline analyst
stages.detail: Parse 835 records, verify initial remittances, maintain business-day calendars, preserve negotiation delivery evidence, and prepare eligible batches. Escalate missing plan documentation before filing costs are committed.

stages.label: Clinical evidence specialist
stages.detail: Connect chart-supported acuity and complexity to permitted offer factors, redact unnecessary information, and inspect licensed data extracts for prohibited benchmarks. The owner checks submission authority and final packet quality.

stages.label: Operations and collections lead
stages.detail: Take ownership of capacity planning, payer payment follow-up, determination-date tracking, and cash reconciliation. Monitor the applicable 30-calendar-day payment obligation after determination separately from actual collection performance.

stages.label: Remittance quality specialist
stages.detail: Independently match bank receipts, corrected remittances, entity refunds, and provider allocations. Sample earned contingency calculations for duplicate collections, baseline-payment leakage, and double-counted case costs.

diagrams.title: Allocate $25,000 Without Confusing Reserves with Expense
diagrams.subtitle: Four capital buckets within the $10,000–$45,000 startup range.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Illustrative startup allocation totals $25,000, within the canonical $10,000–$45,000 range. Shares are 26%, 22%, 32%, and 20%. Capital allocations are not automatically current-period expenses. First-deal timing is 1–4 months; first cash collection can occur later, so maintain a dated liquidity forecast.
diagrams.caption: $6,500 + $5,500 + $8,000 + $5,000 = $25,000. Release filing liquidity only for screened cases with documented fee ownership and reimbursement treatment.

stages.label: Secure intake infrastructure
stages.detail: Fund encrypted storage setup, role-based access, audit logging, 835 parser validation, and backup restoration testing. Use synthetic or de-identified fixtures until contracts and required business-associate arrangements cover the production data path.

stages.label: Contracts and operating setup
stages.detail: Fund provider engagement terms, BAA preparation, representation scope, insurance deposits, and accounting design. Specify the incremental-cash baseline, cost deductions, refund allocation, retained share, and handling of provider-owned money.

stages.label: Case-fee liquidity reserve
stages.detail: Reserve cash for authorized administrative and entity fee outlays where the provider contract assigns funding responsibility. Track advances, reimbursements, losses, and actual refunds separately; a refundable deposit is not earned operator revenue.

stages.label: Acquisition and runway reserve
stages.detail: Fund targeted provider outreach, pilot onboarding, and a limited operating buffer. At the illustrative $5,500 monthly fixed overhead, this bucket alone covers less than one month; use staged spending, provider-funded fees, or additional capital before expanding.

diagrams.title: Thirty Days to a Controlled Recovery Pipeline
diagrams.subtitle: Build a working operation without compressing statutory calendars.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Sprint days are calendar-day project milestones; statutory business-day and calendar-day clocks remain separate. The canonical first-deal horizon is 1–4 months, and this sprint does not assume a completed award, payer deposit, or earned contingency within 30 days.
diagrams.caption: End the month with authorized intake, defensible routing, tested timers, and claim-level economics. Advance individual cases only when their actual statutory and operational conditions hold.

stages.label: Days 1-7
stages.detail: Execute provider engagement and required BAA documents; define the incremental-cash fee formula and fee ownership. Configure least-privilege access and reconcile a sample 835 to bank receipts. Deliver an intake checklist and a tested initial-payment ledger.

stages.label: Days 8-14
stages.detail: Classify a pilot cohort using plan documents, service facts, and state-law applicability. Test holiday handling, 30-business-day negotiation calculations, four-business-day initiation windows, and cooling-off restrictions. Deliver a dated routing record for every pilot claim.

stages.label: Days 15-21
stages.detail: Start eligible open negotiations within their actual deadlines, retain delivery evidence, and prepare supported offers. Test packet generation with clinical source links and prohibited-benchmark checks. Older eligible matters may advance only if their own clocks permit.

stages.label: Days 22-30
stages.detail: Reconcile pilot status, fee exposure, available liquidity, and contractor capacity. Test contingency calculations against partial collections, losses, and confirmed refunds. Deliver a cash forecast and next-month case schedule; record pending negotiations without fabricating awards or collections.
